tools.name: analyze_ab_test
tools.description:
Analyze an A/B test with rate/proportion metrics (e.g. conversion rate, click-through rate).
Uses a Z-test for proportions. Returns significance, p-value, confidence intervals, and lift.

Example: "Control had 5000 visitors with 250 conversions, variant had 5000 visitors with 300 conversions"

control_users.description: Number of users/visitors in the control group

control_conversions.description: Number of conversions in the control group

variant_users.description: Number of users/visitors in the variant group

variant_conversions.description: Number of conversions in the variant group

test_type.description: Two-sided tests for any difference, one-sided for improvement only. Default: two-sided

non_inferiority_margin.description: Non-inferiority margin as a RELATIVE percentage of the control rate (e.g. 2 means the variant may be up to 2% of the control rate worse: at an 80% control rate that is 1.6 percentage points, not 2 points). When > 0, a one-sided non-inferiority test is run and test_type is ignored. Default: 0 (superiority test)

expected_control_share.description: Optional planned share of users in control, as a decimal, for intentionally unequal splits (e.g. 0.05 for a 5% holdout). When set, the response includes a sample ratio mismatch check against this planned split. Analyse the real user counts; never rescale a group to equal size.

tools.name: analyze_ab_test_average
tools.description:
Analyze an A/B test with continuous/average metrics (e.g. revenue per user, time on page, order value).
Uses Welch's T-test (unequal variances), which stays accurate when groups differ in size or spread (e.g. 95/5 holdouts). Returns significance, p-value, confidence intervals, and lift.

Example: "Control had 1000 users with mean $45.20 (std $12.50), variant had 1000 users with mean $48.80 (std $13.10)"

control_users.description: Number of users in the control group (at least 2)

control_mean.description: Mean value for the control group

control_std_dev.description: Standard deviation for the control group

variant_users.description: Number of users in the variant group (at least 2)

variant_mean.description: Mean value for the variant group

variant_std_dev.description: Standard deviation for the variant group

test_type.description: Two-sided or one-sided test. Default: two-sided

non_inferiority_margin.description: Non-inferiority margin as a RELATIVE percentage of the control mean (e.g. 2 means the variant mean may be up to 2% of the control mean lower). When > 0, a one-sided non-inferiority test is run and test_type is ignored. Default: 0 (superiority test)

expected_control_share.description: Optional planned share of users in control, as a decimal, for intentionally unequal splits (e.g. 0.05 for a 5% holdout). When set, the response includes a sample ratio mismatch check against this planned split. Analyse the real user counts; never rescale a group to equal size.

tools.name: calculate_sample_size
tools.description:
Calculate the required sample size for an A/B test.
Supports both rate metrics (conversion rate) and average metrics (revenue per user).
Accounts for multiple variants and Šidák correction.

Example: "How many users do I need to detect a 10% relative lift on a 5% baseline conversion rate?"

metric_type.description: Type of metric: "rate" for proportions (e.g. conversion rate), "average" for continuous metrics (e.g. revenue)

baseline.description: Baseline value. For rate: as percentage (e.g. 5 for 5%). For average: the mean value.

mde.description: Minimum detectable effect as relative percentage lift (e.g. 10 for 10% relative lift)

std_dev.description: Standard deviation (required for average metrics, ignored for rate metrics)

num_variants.description: Number of variant groups (not counting control). Default: 1

daily_traffic.description: Daily traffic to estimate test duration in days

control_share.description: Planned share of traffic in control, as a decimal, for unequal splits (e.g. 0.05 for a 5% holdout, 0.95 for a 5% canary variant). Omit for an equal split.

tools.name: calculate_mde
tools.description:
Calculate the minimum detectable effect (MDE) given a fixed sample size.
Answers: "With this much traffic, what's the smallest effect I can reliably detect?"

Example: "I have 50,000 total users and a 5% conversion rate. What's my MDE?"

baseline.description: Baseline rate as percentage (e.g. 5 for 5%) or baseline mean

std_dev.description: Standard deviation. Required for average metrics. For rate metrics, auto-calculated from baseline if omitted.

control_share.description: Share of total traffic in control, as a decimal, for unequal splits (e.g. 0.05 for a 5% holdout). Omit for an equal split.

tools.name: bayesian_ab_test
tools.description:
Run Bayesian A/B test analysis. Returns probability to be best, expected loss, credible intervals,
and the lift of every variant vs the control (first variant).
Supports both rate metrics (Beta-Binomial model) and average metrics (Normal model).
Supports multiple variants.

Units: for rate metrics, raw values (posterior_mean, credible_interval, expected_loss, absolute lift) are
proportions (0.05 = 5%), so a difference of 0.0006 is 0.06 percentage points. For average metrics they are
in the metric's own units. Each variant also includes expected_loss_display in plain terms.
Expected loss = the average amount you give up by shipping that variant if it is not actually the best.
A common stopping rule: ship when the leader's expected loss is below the smallest difference you care about.

Example: "Control: 5000 visitors, 250 conversions. Variant: 5000 visitors, 300 conversions."

metric_type.description: Metric type: "rate" for proportions, "average" for continuous

variants.description: Array of variants. First is treated as control.

prior_alpha.description: Beta prior alpha (rate metrics only). Default: 1 (uniform prior)

prior_beta.description: Beta prior beta (rate metrics only). Default: 1 (uniform prior)

tools.name: check_srm
tools.description:
Check for Sample Ratio Mismatch (SRM) in an A/B test.
SRM occurs when the traffic split between control and variant doesn't match the planned ratio (50/50 unless you say otherwise).
SRM is a sign of a bug in the experiment setup and invalidates results.
For intentionally unequal splits (holdouts, canary tests) pass the planned control share, e.g. 0.05 for a 5% holdout.

Example: "Control has 10,234 users, variant has 9,766 users"

control_users.description: Number of users in the control group

variant_users.description: Number of users in the variant group

expected_control_share.description: Planned share of users in control, as a decimal. 0.5 for 50/50, 0.1 for a 10% holdout, 0.95 for a 5% canary variant. Default: 0.5

tools.name: paired_test
tools.description:
Run a paired test for before/after or matched-pair data.
Automatically selects between Paired T-Test (if data is normal) and Wilcoxon Signed-Rank Test (if not).
Uses bootstrap resampling + Jarque-Bera test to check normality.

Example: "Before: [10, 12, 8, 15, 11], After: [12, 14, 9, 18, 13]"

sample_before.description: Array of measurements before treatment (or group A)

sample_after.description: Array of measurements after treatment (or group B). Must be same length as sample_before.

tools.name: survey_sample_size
tools.description:
Calculate the required number of completed survey responses using Cochran's formula with finite population correction.
Optionally pass expected_response_rate to get how many people to invite.

Example: "How many responses do I need from a population of 10,000 with 5% margin of error at 95% confidence?"

margin_of_error.description: Desired margin of error as percentage (e.g. 5 for ±5%)

expected_response_rate.description: Optional: expected survey response rate as percentage (e.g. 20 for 20%). When given, returns how many people to invite to get the required completed responses.
